chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Hassan ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
He said: I asked him about the Night of Power, so he said: Seek it on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third.
ai.seo_question: Which nights of Ramadan are specified for seeking Laylat al-Qadr in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the nights of the 21st and 23rd of Ramadan as the primary candidates for Laylat al-Qadr, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus that emphasizes these specific nights based on the Imam's explicit instruction. It underscores the tradition of seeking the night during the odd nights of the last ten days, a practice deeply rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance and distinct from some Sunni traditions that focus more broadly on the final ten days. This hadith serves as a foundational jurisprudential reference for determining the precise timing of this significant night of worship and divine decree.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 20-8 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hikam, on the authority of Sayf ibn Umayrih, on the authority of Hisan ibn Mihran, “I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) about the Night of Power. The Imam (MGB) said, ‘Seek it on the nights of the twenty-first and the twenty-third of Ramazan.’”
